entries.title: Trump Says He’ll be More Productive With a Democratic Congress
entries.summary: Citing his history as a businessman, Trump said that he would use his veto powers to force both parties to compromise.
entries.content:
President Donald Trump predicted that the next two years of his presidency would be “unbelievably productive” because he plans to leverage his veto powers to force deals with the incoming Democratic congressional majorities.

The comments were an abrupt about-face from his campaign season diatribes against his Democratic rivals, whom he called “crazy” and insinuated that they were intentionally trying to hurt the country.

In a Wednesday interview on Fox News from Shenzhen, China, the president said he has been “called by many Democrats” seeking legislative deals — which he said planned to negotiate in good faith. Citing his history as a businessman, Trump added that he would use his veto powers to force both parties to compromise.

“I think in many ways I can do better now” than when Republicans controlled Congress, the president said.

“And I have a feeling that this is going to be an unbelievably productive two years,” he added.

Trump also told reporters he would welcome Democrats to the White House to discuss policy deals.

“They will send me a bill on health care and I’ll say no way. They will call me and sit down. That’s what I do,” he said.
entries.author: Gavin J. Quinton

entries.title: Wizards Snap Losing Streak With a 103-99 Win Over the Raptors
entries.summary: Anthony Davis had 25 points and 14 rebounds, while rookie AJ Dybantsa added 23 and 12 in a much-needed victory.
entries.content:
TORONTO — Anthony Davis had 25 points and 14 rebounds, rookie AJ Dybantsa added 23 points and 12 boards, and the Washington Wizards beat the undermanned Toronto Raptors 103-99 on Wednesday night to snap an eight-game losing streak.

Canadian Kyshawn George added 20 points for the Wizards, who got off to a promising 4-3 start but hadn’t won since. His 3-pointer with 8:55 left in the fourth capped an 11-0 Wizards run that made it 91-82, Washington’s biggest lead to that point of the game.

Immanuel Quickley scored 24 points and Jamison Battle added 19, including five 3-pointers, as Toronto lost its sixth straight.

RJ Barrett (right hamstring tightness) and Scottie Barnes (left groin injury management) were ruled out for the game hours before tipoff, joining superstar Kawhi Leonard (left knee injury management) on the Raptors’ injury report.

Things got worse for Toronto in the second quarter when Collin Murray-Boyles left the game with an undisclosed illness. He had one point, two rebounds and an assist in five minutes of play as the Raptors’ starting power forward.

Toronto was a dismal 7 for 14 at the free throw line, struggling for the third game in a row. The Raptors were 10 for 19 (52.6%) in Sunday’s 112-108 loss to the New York Knicks and 10 for 18 (55.6%) on Tuesday in a 111-102 loss to New York.

Up Next

The Wizards visit the Chicago Bulls on Friday for an NBA Cup game.
entries.author: The Associated Press

entries.title: Mark Ein Takes Over Rock Creek Tennis Center, Plans a $25 Million Renovation
entries.summary: The local entrepreneur struck a 60-year lease agreement with the Interior Department to operate the home of the D.C. Open.
entries.content:
Local entrepreneur Mark Ein’s Rollingwood Sports struck a 60-year lease agreement with the Interior Department to operate Rock Creek Tennis Center, home of the Mubadala D.C. Open, the company announced Thursday.

The lease also comes with a $25 million commitment to renovate the center, including rebuilding the 25 courts, plus adding three new ones. Court lighting, public restrooms, concessions facilities, HVAC systems and the center’s stadium will be refurbished, along with the locker rooms, which will be opened to the public for the first time, the announcement said. The overhaul will be supported in part by a $9.6 million investment from the D.C. Council.

"Our goal is to make the Rock Creek Tennis Center one of the very best public urban tennis and recreation facilities in America and deliver something extraordinary for the District and our region,” said Ein, who’s also a minority owner of the Washington Commanders. “We are going to make the investments that this historic facility has needed for decades, create more opportunities for people to play tennis and other sports year-round, and ensure one of the world’s great professional tennis tournaments stays in Washington, DC.”

Rollingwood Sports, which operates the D.C. Open, said the renovations will cement the tournament's future at the facility. After next year's competition, the timeworn indoor tennis bubble will be replaced.

Select tennis courts will also be lined for pickleball use, and there are plans to construct a facility for high school and college competition and training. Renderings shared Thursday also show remade soccer fields north of the facility and no changes made to on-site parking.

Rollingwood Sports previously held short-term leases at the tennis center and said it’s being supported in the renovation by various interest groups, including Events D.C., Howard University and the Washington Tennis & Education Foundation, which used to hold its events at the tennis center before relocating 15 years ago because of poor conditions.

The foundation — the nonprofit beneficiary of the D.C. Open — will get its own campus at Rock Creek to complement its current facilities in Ward 7, the announcement said, allowing its tuition-free programming for D.C. students to grow from 700 students to 1,000.

“We see Rock Creek as a year-round home for both professional tennis and community programs — where children learn and develop their tennis game, where families connect with one another, and where the Mubadala DC Open continues to inspire new generations of life champions each year,” foundation CEO Candace Smith said in a statement.

The renovation garnered support from local tennis professionals Frances Tiafoe and Hailey Baptiste, who frequently play at the D.C. Open. Both praised the investment in keeping world-class tennis accessible for kids in the District.

“I know first-hand how important this tennis center and the tournament are for our community,” Tiafoe, a Hyattsville native, said in a statement. “Getting this facility finally fixed and making sure the historic tournament can stay in DC for decades to come is incredibly important to me and lots of other kids like me.”
entries.author: Kendall Staton

entries.title: Trinity Rodman Is the Spirit’s Lone NWSL Award Winner
entries.summary: Despite earning a spot in Saturday’s NWSL championship match, Washington landed just one player on the league’s Best XI or Second XI.
entries.content:
The Washington Spirit have had a successful season by just about every metric. On Saturday, it will face the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship match — the franchise’s third straight appearance in the league finals.

The team’s success in the regular season was powered by a number of standout players, but it will come away from the year with only so much hardware to show for that.

On Wednesday, the league announced its year-end honorees at the NWSL Awards, held at George Washington University’s Lisner Auditorium. Forward Trinity Rodman was the lone Spirit player honored as part of the NWSL’s Best XI, which recognizes the top players at their respective positions. The Spirit had no players named to the Second XI, either.

Rodman was also a finalist for MVP after scoring 11 goals while assisting on eight more in 29 matches.

North Carolina Courage forward Ashley Sanchez earned MVP after tying the NWSL record for regular season goals with 20. Sanchez originally began her career with the Spirit and played in Washington from 2020 to 2023 before being traded to North Carolina in January 2024.

Croix Bethune, who the Spirit will face on Saturday, was named midfielder of the year after setting a new league record for assists with 11.

Denver’s Janine Sonis was named defender of the year, and Utah’s Jimmy Coenraets was named coach of the year. Outside of the Best XI, Gotham FC was the only club with multiple award winners, with Jordynn Dudley winning rookie of the year and Ann-Katrin Berger winning goalkeeper of the year.
entries.author: Alex Schiffer

entries.title: Conservative ‘Dark Money’ Giant Reports Record Giving
entries.summary: The group, DonorsTrust, boosted several Trump-aligned nonprofits in 2025, according to previously unreported tax filings.
entries.content:
Conservative “dark money” organization DonorsTrust distributed $447 million in grants to hundreds of nonprofit organizations during 2025, including numerous groups aligned with President Donald Trump, according to its previously unreported tax filing.

That’s a record for the donor-advised fund, which said that it has spread more than $2.5 billion in donor funds over more than 25 years in business.

Lawson Bader, president and CEO of DonorsTrust, said in a statement to The Washington Sun that he expects DonorsTrust’s grantmaking to grow in the coming years and that the “marketplace has changed dramatically,” with more people knowing what donor-advised funds are — and utilizing them.

Through DonorsTrust, wealthy individuals have steered money to political organizations, think tanks, churches, universities, hospitals, museums, news organizations and other nonprofits. Among them: groups that attempt to influence politics and policymakers, which is why donor-advised funds such as DonorsTrust have drawn criticism from transparency advocates and lawmakers including Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-Rhode Island) for obscuring the ultimate source of the grants.

“Ah yes, the infamous ‘dark money’ label. I once attended a Halloween party dressed as ‘dark money.’ Nobody got the joke,” Bader wrote.

In its mission statement, DonorsTrust tells patrons it “protects your charitable intent, preserves your privacy, and ensures your giving aligns with your conservative, libertarian, or faith-based values — now and for generations to come.”

A self-described “donor privacy purist,” Bader draws a distinction between political campaign spending and charitable giving by donor-advised funds such as DonorsTrust that “do not make grants to support political candidates or election campaigns.”

Bader called it “difficult to generalize” the motivations behind the record giving, although he did note an uptick in gifts to religious groups. He also cautioned against interpreting the increase in grantmaking in 2025, the first year of Trump’s second term, “as a reflection of the political environment.”

Several Trump-aligned groups, which are dedicated to developing and implementing his “America first” vision, received financial boosts through DonorsTrust, which are anonymous to the public.

DonorsTrust disclosed steering more than $2.8 million in 2025 to America First Policy Institute, a policy research institute founded by now-Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins. That includes $2.5 million “to support the Media Campaign for America 250,” the nation’s semiquincentennial celebration, according to the filing.

America First Policy Institute led the America 250 Civics Education Coalition, a partnership with the Department of Education, to promote “patriotic” civics education around the country’s 250th birthday this summer. Ben Judge, who chairs the board of the America First Policy Institute, co-chaired the coalition.

Judge is also president of The America Fund, which received more than $3 million through DonorsTrust for “general operations” in 2025. The foundation focuses on the “identification and analysis of the activities that best preserve the American way of life,” according to its website, which includes “Victory Reports” on conservative efforts that include an ultimately unsuccessful case against birthright citizenship making it to the Supreme Court.

“However, the loss at the Court does not diminish the case study’s central lesson: a constitutional argument dismissed for decades as a fringe legal theory forced a Supreme Court confrontation, produced four dissents on the merits of the constitutional question, and remains ripe for future litigation,” America Fund wrote in a one-page “victory report” on the birthright citizenship case.

America First Legal, a nonprofit law firm co-founded by now-White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, received $471,000 from DonorsTrust in 2025. That includes $50,000 “to support election integrity and the prevention of government overreach" and $7,000 “to support their work on the 2020 Census,” according to DonorsTrust’s tax return.

Rollins and Miller each received six-figure bonuses from their respective nonprofits in 2024 before joining the second Trump administration, The Sun previously reported.

America First Legal, America First Policy Institute and America Fund did not respond to requests for comment.

Other organizations that received grants through DonorsTrust last year and were influential in Washington include the Ethics and Public Policy Center, which published a bombshell — and highly criticized — report on the dangers of abortion drug mifepristone last year. The Ethics and Public Policy Center, which studies a range of “moral” policy issues, received $1.4 million through DonorsTrust in 2025 “for general operations.”

Other organizations that backed efforts to revoke the Food and Drug Administration approval of mifepristone, citing the Ethics and Public Policy Center report, also received grants through DonorsTrust: The Susan B. Anthony List Education Fund received $1 million, and the Heritage Foundation received a combined $910,000 in grants.

Students for Fair Admissions, a nonprofit that won a Supreme Court case in 2023 striking down affirmative action in university admissions, got $475,120 for “general operations.”

The Young Americans for Liberty Foundation, which funds the grassroots Young Americans for Liberty, received more than $1.3 million.

And dark money groups tied to judicial activist Leonard Leo — a member of the board of the Ethics and Public Policy Center — got big grants, including nearly $3.7 to Teneo Network and $7.6 million to Consumers’ Research.

But, as Bader noted, the donations spanned the nonprofit spectrum and hundreds of organizations received grants through DonorsTrust last year.

The Daily Caller News Foundation received $1.2 million. Breitbart News Foundation got $800,000. The University of Chicago received nearly $1.3 million for a professor fund. The Wounded Warrior Project received $13,400. In Northern Virginia, the Wolf Trap Foundation for the Performing Arts received $50,000 for its annual gala. And humanitarian organization Samaritan’s Purse received $5 million for U.S. hurricane relief.

When The Sun asked about how Democrats’ focus on reining in “dark money” in the next Congress could affect the organization, Bader called it “a mistake to assume that attacks on donor privacy are exclusively a Democratic concern,” citing the Trump administration and Republicans’ attacks on left-leaning nonprofits including Democratic megadonor George Soros’ Open Society Foundations and the Southern Poverty Law Center.

“Whether someone supports a public policy organization, a mosque, an art museum, or a rehabilitation center, I believe the principle of donor privacy deserves protection,” Bader wrote. “That principle should apply regardless of which political party happens to control Congress or the White House.”
entries.author: Taylor Giorno
